ambiguities: T2 alert side: the plan says 'difference of mean excess between the alerts and the control entries (..., one mean per event and stratum)'. Read first as alert cells (class_cells, all class entries, one mean per event and stratum): C1 gave -0.04692 against -0.05492 published, and every class differed. Chosen reading: the alerts are the one-per-event alerts of alerts.jsonl (the plan's unit of every test), placed in the stratum of their own price and hours to the scheduled end; the controls are one mean per event and stratum. The chosen reading reproduces the published T2 difference of every class to < 1e-7.

T2 combination across strata: the plan does not give the weights. Chosen: mean over alerts of (alert excess minus the mean of the control cell means of its stratum), i.e. strata weighted by their number of alert events. Weighting by entries or unweighted strata gave different numbers (diagnostic run, not kept).

T2 controls: base cell minus class cells minus excluded cells. class_cells holds the alerts and the refused alerts of a class (amendment 001), so refused alerts are neither alerts nor controls. Reproduces the published control counts exactly.

Strata bounds on ties (price exactly 0.10/0.25/0.50/0.75, hours exactly 24/168/720): the plan gives cuts only. Chosen: band = number of cuts strictly below the value (a cut belongs to the lower band); this is what the exported cells show on the 19 single-entry events whose price sits on a cut.

T2 resampling: events drawn with replacement among all events of validation_info with an eligible entry (base_cells, 1406); escalation draws are fresh draws, not added to the 2,000; an undefined resample (no alert drawn) counts as a hit; an alert whose stratum has no control in a resample is left out of that resample.

Excess interval: the plan gives neither the number of draws nor the interval method. Chosen: 10,000 draws, percentile interval with linear interpolation; one alert per event, so resampling events = resampling alerts.

Verdict 'under the corrected threshold' read as strict p < 0.05 / N; a T2 p with 0 hits is replaced by its bound 3/draws; SUPPORTED needs excess >= 0.05; NOT_SPECIFIC uses the T1 p of the same class on validation_public_process.

Alerted entries: the export gives entries only through class_cells, which also hold refused alerts (amendment 001); for C7 it gives 524 entries where the registry and RESULTS.md give 519. Not derivable from the export; reported, not gated. Entries are not exported for discovery_info and validation_public_process.

Sweep halves and robustness halves: 'cut at the median alert time' read as t < median vs t >= median of the class's own validation alerts. 'Median hours from alert to real close' read as the upper median (median_high): the plain median gives 497.8 / 523.5 / 527.2 for C1 / C2 / C3 against 499 / 528 / 529 published, the upper median matches all four. 'Calendar weeks' read as 7-day blocks from the Unix epoch (t // 604800): ISO weeks gave a C2 upper bound of +12.6 against +10.9 published and C3 -5.0 to +2.6 against -6.1 to +3.4; epoch blocks agree within Monte-Carlo error. 'Entry of 5,000 USD or more' is not derivable: the published n (105 for C1) exceeds the earliest alerts of 5,000 USD or more (43), so the variant re-derives the earliest alert among large entries, and alerts.jsonl keeps only the earliest alert of each event; reported, not gated. 'Alert events a week' read as events / ((last alert t - first alert t) / 7 days). 'Strictly before the scheduled end' read as hours_to_end > 0; 'at least 24 h before the real close' as hours_before_real_close >= 24; 'entry of 5,000 USD or more' as entry_usd >= 5000; 'price a follower paid' as win - follow_price over alerts with a follower price <= 0.90; weeks = ISO calendar week of the alert time (UTC).
